tactic.name: Induce enemy dragon retaliation to damage its own rear stack
tactic.goal: Trade a small legal melee attack for collateral damage to the dragon's allied stack
tactic.mechanism_claim: A breath-capable dragon can damage a stack behind its melee target while retaliating
preconditions: Breath-capable dragon; not Bone/Ghost/Crystal/Faerie dragon merely because its name contains dragon
The dragon can retaliate and survives the provoking strike
Attacker permits retaliation; a no-enemy-retaliation creature is not a valid trigger
Legal adjacent attack destination lies between dragon and the dragon's allied rear stack
Correct axial attack vector and two-hex footprint; enumerate rather than guess from screenshot
operation_order: Construct a legal battle state containing enemy dragon, enemy rear stack and a provoking allied stack
Enumerate legal AMOVE attacks and inspect actual affected stack IDs
Execute the candidate attack; require a retaliation event and damage on dragon's own rear stack
Replay identical seed with a geometry control that moves the rear stack outside the breath vector
Compare own casualty value and enemy collateral damage; do not assume the tactic improves the entire battle
failure_conditions: Wrong breath vector or two-hex side ambiguity
Friendly rear stack is absent from second hex
Counterdamage costs more than the collateral benefit
Opponent moves rear stack or attacks proactively
tactic.offense: Choose legal geometry that induces advantageous enemy friendly fire
tactic.defense: Keep vulnerable allied stacks outside own dragon retaliation vectors, or deny the provoking attack
tactic.generality: Rule-based tactical mechanism; distinct from a particular legacy AI valuation exploit
tactic.countermeasure_source_location: same section, following paragraph beginning Conversely, when using your own dragons
tactic.reconstruction_policy: Coordinates, counts, heroes and seeds supplied by the lab are experimental reconstructions, never presented as extracted human actions
